title: Typical or forced: couplings and field contracts of the made field

key_results.statement: Class C, test body, for $C_{\rm eff}$: effective level-$k$ blocks $B_{x,k}=M_k\sigma_3+\gamma N(x)W_k+E_\varphi$, $W_k=f_k\sigma_3+g_k\mathbb 1_2+h_{1,k}\sigma_1+h_{2,k}\sigma_2$, hopping $\tau_{x,x+1;k}=\tau(1+\gamma b_k\bar N_x)$.
R3 holds at every place in every field state iff $(f,g,h_1,h_2)=(\alpha,\beta,\eta_1,\eta_2)(m\mathbb 1_N+D)$ with $b$ free; then $\Gamma(x)=\gamma\Delta N(x)W_*$.

For $C_{\rm eff}$ (exact in $\gamma N_0$, first order in the gradients): the start at $p=0$ has velocity $v_{k,\sigma}(0)=-\sigma\tau_k\gamma N_0h_{1,k}/\lvert\mathbf d_k(0)\rvert=-\sigma\tau\gamma N_0h_{1,k}/M_k+O(\gamma^2)$ (at rest in every state iff $h_1=0$); for $h_1=0$ the fall is $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=-\tau_k^2(\sigma v_k'+\tilde\mu_k')/\tilde\mu_k$.

At first order in $\gamma$, $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=-\tau^2\gamma N'(f_k+\sigma g_k)/M_k+O(\gamma^2)$; R3, rest at $p=0$ and a fall equal across levels and both branches in every field state hold iff the coupling is in $\mathcal S_1$: $h_1=0$, $g=0$, $(f,h_2)=(\alpha,\eta_2)(m\mathbb 1_N+D)$, $b$ free, with $a=-\tau^2\gamma\alpha N'+O(\gamma^2)$; the larger set $\mathcal S_1^{\pm}$ ($\beta$ free) has $a_{k,\sigma}=-\tau^2\gamma N'(\alpha+\sigma\beta)$, branch-dependent iff $\beta\neq0$; coupling (r) lies outside.

In class C of dimension $5N$: $\dim\mathcal S_{\rm R3}=N+4$, $\dim\mathcal S_1^{\pm}=N+3$, $\dim\mathcal S_1=N+2$, $\dim\mathcal S_2=1$; for $N\ge2$ all are nowhere dense and of measure zero (exceptional), and the language does not select them within class C.

First order in $\gamma$ and in a deviation from $P_0\in\mathcal S_1$: R3 defect $\gamma\Delta N(x)\delta W_k$ (exact); rest defect $v_{k,\sigma}(0)=-\sigma\tau\gamma N_0\delta h_{1,k}/M_k$; fall $a_{k,\sigma}(0)=-\tau^2\gamma N'[\alpha+(\delta f_k+\sigma\delta g_k)/M_k]$; $\delta b$ and $\delta h_2$ do not enter at order $\gamma$.

Every member of class F, lowest state at grid momentum $k_L$: $\chi_0(x,y)=\frac{2n}{\lvert X_f\rvert}\sum_q\cos(q\cdot d)S_L(q)$, $S_L(q)=\langle w_L\vert\phi(h(k_L+q)-\epsilon_L)^{-1}\phi\vert w_L\rangle\ge0$ for $q\neq0$; made field $N(y)=n\bar\phi_L-g\chi_0(y,x_s)+O(g^2)$ at fixed $L$ for $\lvert g\rvert<\Delta_L/(2N_f\lVert\phi\rVert)$.
If the made field is short range, $S_{L,\rm e}(q)=\frac12(S_L(q)+S_L(-q))$ is bounded uniformly in $L$ and in the grid momenta $q\neq0$.

On G1, $S=\lvert F\rvert^2/(\epsilon_0(k_0+q)-\epsilon_0)+S_{\rm an}$ with analytic $\lvert F\rvert^2$, $S_{\rm an}$, $\lvert F(0)\rvert^2=\bar\phi^2$; for $k_0=0$, if the even part of $S$ is analytic at $q=0$, the made field is short range uniformly in $L$.

On $U$ (G1 and $\bar\phi\neq0$) the made field is long range for every $k_0$; for $L\to\infty$ along sides with $L\lvert k_L-k_0\rvert\to0$ at fixed $y,y'$: $\chi_0(y,x_s)-\chi_0(y',x_s)=2n\bar\phi^2[\mathcal G_A(y-x_s)-\mathcal G_A(y'-x_s)]+R$ (linear, logarithmic, $1/\lvert d\rvert$ in $D=1,2,3$); for $r=1$ every member of class F with $\phi\neq0$ is long range.

In the Euclidean topology of the coefficient space, $U\cap{\rm F}$ is open and dense in class F and its complement (G1 fails or $\bar\phi=0$) is closed in F with empty interior: long range is typical, short range exceptional; on G1 short range requires $\bar\phi=0$.

Inside the complement, for G1 with $k_0=0$ and $\bar\phi=0$ (not a classification): short range in $D=1$; in $D=2,3$ $\chi_0=-2n\sum C_{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\mathcal G_A+c_L+O(\lvert d\rvert^{-D-1})$ as $L\to\infty$, a $\lvert d\rvert^{-D}$ power law unless $C=cA$ ($C=0$ for $D=3$).

On G1, long range follows from $\Phi_x$ carrying the density of the conserved number of field objects (gapless band) in the lowest state, $\bar\phi\neq0$, M6-invariantly $\lim_{L\to\infty}\lvert X_f\rvert N_f^{-1/2}\lvert\langle\varphi_{q_L}\vert\Phi_x\vert\varphi_0\rangle\rvert\neq0$; on G1, sufficient for short range for every $k_0$: a conserved charge $\sum_jZ^{(j)}$ that $\Phi_x$ changes within the lowest sector (Z).

Short-range member of class F: $r=2$, $h=(C_1+2Dt_f)\otimes\mathbb 1_2+\Delta\mathbb 1\otimes\lvert2\rangle\langle2\rvert$, $\phi=\sigma_1$; in $D=1$ $\chi_0=\frac{n}{t_f\sinh\kappa}\cosh\kappa(\frac L2-d)/\sinh\frac{\kappa L}2$, $\cosh\kappa=1+\Delta/(2t_f)$; in every $D$ exponentially bounded uniformly in $L$.

open_issues: Members of class F in the complement of U are not classified (allowed by the question's dated note): degenerate, quartic or multiple minima for r ≥ 2, φ̄ = 0 with k0 ≠ 0, and φ̄ = 0, C = cA in D = 2, 3; condition (Z) is only sufficient.
The made field is the finite-L Taylor coefficient; its convergence radius Δ_L/(2N_f‖φ‖) shrinks as L^−2 on G1, and no statement uniform in L beyond χ0 is derived.

Item 1 is at first order in γ, at the band point p = 0 and first order in the gradients; the order γ² (where b and h2 enter the fall) needs the body's own change of the field and is not treated; p = π is not treated; T3 is assumed for the field of 04-profile.
Exceptional and typical refer to the Euclidean topology of the coefficient spaces of classes C and F; the language supplies no measure on descriptions.
